---
title: "Engineer course setup"
subtitle: "One locked environment and one clean kernel per Chapter"
format: html
---

Clone the current development course, install its locked environment, and
start Jupyter from the repository root:

```bash
git clone --branch develop --single-branch https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scnsim.git
cd scnsim
uv sync --locked
uv run --with jupyterlab jupyter lab
```

The `jupyterlab` package is ephemeral tooling for that command; it is not added
to SCNSim or its lock. An editor-provided Jupyter frontend may instead open the
Chapter Notebook after `uv sync --locked`. Select the repository's `.venv`
Python kernel, restart it, and use **Run All**.

Chapters 1–4 form the mainline course; Chapters 5–8 are optional
continuations. Chapters 1–7 are separate clean-kernel execution units.
Chapter 8 instead has
an explicit two-kernel procedure: execute Lesson 1, stop that kernel, then use
a second fresh kernel to run only Lesson 2 against the same preserved working
directory. The shorter web Lessons are reading views over ordered source
fragments and are not independently runnable.

On a cold machine, the first numerical request may prepare the locked Julia
runtime and take longer than later requests. A relative path such as
`workspaces/engineer-chapter-02` is resolved from the process's current working
directory. That workspace is Result evidence, not a disposable calculation
cache: ignoring it in Git neither deletes nor backs it up, and exact later
resolution requires its preserved bytes.

For ordinary design iteration, classify the change before reusing a workspace.
A new `ParameterSet` reuses the same captured Plan, Run, and Views. Changing an
objective expression, comparison, target, scale, or weight constructs a new
`OptimizationSpec` on those same objects. Changing model defaults, topology,
Ports, or a captured parameter definition requires rebuilding the inputs,
Plan, Run, Views, and Specs. A newly rebuilt Plan's old View or ParameterRef is
foreign even when a Python name or printed declaration looks the same.

With `versioned=False`, constructing that different Plan at the same workspace
path deliberately replaces the prior active Plan evidence; it does not erase
all evidence on every request. Requests on one Plan remain distinct by their
canonical request identity. Use `versioned=True` when multiple Plan versions
must coexist, and preserve the workspace bytes required by each version.
Reusing the same variable names and workspace path in one live kernel is legal
when the Plan identity is unchanged; a kernel restart is not an identity
operation and does not repair a foreign handle.
